To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel data server system that supports interactive range queries for large multivariate time series data, and we implemented the system on a networked computer cluster and demonstrated that it is scalable to datasets sized hundreds of gigabytes.
our scalable data server system supports interactive range-query selection of arbitrary subsets of multivariate time-varies data and can handle datasets sized at several hundred gigabytes.

our system is capable of supporting interactive visualization of an arbitrary range-query subset of a large multivariable time-varying data set, by employing a set of parallel data servers that are capable of load-balanced distribution of the data, and are capable of supporting a large range of queries with minimal latency.

the following two questions: 1) How to support interactive range-queries on large multivariate datasets, and 2) how to leverage multiple data servers to efficiently answer these range-queries.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a scalable data server system that can efficiently support interactive visualization of a large multivariable time-varying data, using a cluster of networked machines as data servers, and a single client machine for visualization.
we have developed a system that enables interactive visualization of a selected subset of a large multivariable time-varying volume dataset, and that can be scaled to a large number of data servers.
we have developed a system that can support interactive visualization of a large multivarate time-varying data set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given dataset, the scalability of the system is independent of the size and complexity of the data.
, for large datasets, it is more efficient to store and query the data in a distributed fashion than to load the entire dataset in-core.

, by leveraging a large number of parallel data servers, it is possible to support efficient visualization of a large subset of a large multivariable time-varying data, even when that subset is not known in advance.
